request.system: You recommend one pick from this draft board. The board is the world: player_id and every alternative must be a player_id on board. hint_argmax_vols is a calculator, not the answer. If you pick someone else you must set VOLS_DISSENT. If you are not the best available ECR you must set ECR_DISAGREE, and do not pick beyond ecr_best + margin. The board is capped; do not read scarcity from its length. Wait versus take is yours. Set coin_flip when a rerun of this same board could reasonably name a different player. flags is a closed set: ECR_DISAGREE, BYE_STACK, POSITION_RUN, EMPTY_STARTER, UPSIDE, VOLS_DISSENT. When you set VOLS_DISSENT, name hint_argmax_vols's player once in why as "<player> is the VOLS pick", then say why you pass. When you set ECR_DISAGREE, name ecr_best's player once as "<player> is the ECR pick", then say why you pass. Write each label one time. Do not repeat the phrase or restate the pick you passed on. The board is lean. Call detail(player_ids) once for the players you are deciding between to read delta_starter_points, the ECR spread (ecr_min/max/std), gp, points, and bye. Batch every id into that one call. Ids must be on the board.

tools.description: Heavier per-player columns for the players you are deciding between: delta_starter_points, the ECR spread (ecr_min/max/std), gp, points, bye. Batch every id into one call. Ids must be on the board.
tools.name: detail

samples.why: wr-bye-clash is the VOLS pick and wr-bye-clash is the ECR pick, but its week 9 bye lands on the same week my QB, an RB, and my only WR already sit, a week that currently projects just 36 starter points. wr-bye-clear is two ECR spots later with essentially identical production (149 points, 17 games) and a week 5 bye that my roster covers, which is why it nearly triples the starter-point gain (29.0 vs 12.0). WR2 and FLEX are both empty and 17 picks separate me from pick 93, so I take the receiver that actually fills the hole every week.

Week 9 is already a wasteland with QB, RB and WR all idle, and wr-bye-clash is the VOLS pick but shares that same bye, so its 12.0 delta starter points is a mirage. wr-bye-clear lands on bye 5, filling the open WR spot in the weeks that actually hurt, and its 29.0 delta starter points nearly doubles the field. wr-bye-clash is the ECR pick, two spots better and one point higher on the season, which is not worth stacking a fourth body onto the worst week on the schedule. rb-e is redundant behind two rostered backs and adds the least.

My week 9 is already gutted with QB, RB, and WR all on bye, and wr-bye-clash is the VOLS pick and also the ECR pick but it carries that same week 9 bye, which is why its delta_starter_points is only 12.0 while wr-bye-clear delivers 29.0 on nearly identical season points (149.0 vs 150.0) and 17 games. A two-slot ECR gap with identical ecr spread (std 2.0, no range) is noise; the schedule fit is not. This fills the open WR starter and lets a later pick handle FLEX, K, and DEF before pick 93.

My WR2 is empty every week and the FLEX behind it, so a receiver is the pick here. wr-bye-clash is the VOLS pick and also the ECR pick, but it carries a week 9 bye that already guts my lineup (QB, RB, WR all out, 36 starter points); adding a fourth week 9 body there buys almost nothing. wr-bye-clear projects nearly identical season points on 17 games and its week 5 bye lands on a full week, which is why it nearly triples the starter-points gain (29.0 vs 12.0). Two ECR slots of cost for a real weekly upgrade.

My WR2 is open and week 9 is already a wasteland with QB, RB, and WR all on bye. wr-bye-clash is the VOLS pick and wr-bye-clash is the ECR pick, but its bye 9 lands on that same dead week, so its 12.0 delta_starter_points is largely wasted; I pass on a marginal one-slot ECR edge. wr-bye-clear grades at 29.0 added starter points with a bye 5 that lands on an otherwise healthy week, essentially the same season total (149 vs 150 points, 17 gp, tight ECR spread with std 2.0), and fills the empty WR slot. rb-e is a luxury with RB already at 2/2.
